description: Phase 10 A/B corpus manifest. Fixtures are immutable (same discipline as the golden masters). expectedStrings are key-content/reading-order markers expected under BOTH engines; expectedTables gives the row/col shape (header + data rows, excluding the markdown separator line) of tables a correct extraction preserves; diacritics lists strings that must survive verbatim. Known per-engine divergences are documented in notes.

fixtures.notes: Two-column newsletter page. Correct extraction keeps each column's text contiguous and reads the left column before the right column (both engines do: pdfjs by draw order, opendataloader via xycut reading order).

One bordered table (drawn grid: Region/Units/Margin + North/South/West rows) and one borderless table (Product/Price/Stock + Widget/Gadget rows). Known divergence: the drawn grid lines degrade opendataloader's text layer on the bordered table ('West 1430' arrives mangled as 'West 143 0'); pdfjs is unaffected because it reads the text layer only. 'South 950' survives in both. The borderless table renders as a clean 3-line run under both engines (with keepLineBreaks).

expectedStrings: Covenant terms subject to the 2024 restatement.
fixtures.notes: Running header ('CONFIDENTIAL Meridian Annual Review') and footer ('Page N of 2') plus a footnote line, with distinct body text per page. Known divergence: opendataloader EXCLUDES headers/footers by default (includeHeaderFooter defaults to false); pdfjs always includes them. Both behaviors are acceptable for Layer 1; the difference is recorded, not treated as a failure.
Danish text exercising æ/ø/å in both cases (extends the Phase 7 golden-master-da coverage). Correct extraction preserves every diacritic verbatim — Layer 2 evidence is never transliterated.

Dense financial/legal page (the project's target domain): figures, percentages, ISO and long-form dates, company names, and a small segment table (Segment/Revenue/Margin + Nordic/Iberia/DACH rows). Correct extraction preserves every figure verbatim.

Image-only page (embedded PNG of grey 'text' stripes, no text layer) simulating a scan. Documents the OCR gap honestly: BOTH engines extract empty text here (opendataloader's OCR requires the out-of-scope hybrid backend). Empty output is a VALID data point, not a failure.
